name: Elara Petridis
psychographics: Organization-obsessed former athlete who treats the kitchen like a strategy board; she color-codes the calendar and the lunchboxes, but secretly resents the endless spreadsheet work required to keep everyone healthy.
current_solutions: Cozi Family Organizer for scheduling, Yummly for recipe filtering, and a recurring order with HelloFresh (modified meals). She also keeps a handwritten 'Red Book' of safe snacks for the youngest who has celiac disease.
frustration: Last Thursday at 8:30 AM, she was rushing to pack lunches before the school bell. She handed the 10-year-old a muesli bar she bought in good faith, labeled 'gluten-free'. Three bites later, the kid complained it tasted 'off'. Elara checked the fine print later: the bar was manufactured in a facility that processes wheat. She had to drive the kid to school late and call the teacher, feeling guilty for the rest of the day.
decision_style: Researches extensively on parenting forums (Mumsnet equivalents) for 2-3 weeks before trying a new product; once she trusts a brand, she sticks with it religiously, but switching costs feel high.
voice: Rambling but structured, shifts between formal teaching jargon and exhausted mum sighs. 'Look, I just want the morning to run smooth, you know? But sometimes the labels lie, and then it’s a whole thing, ya know?'
